title: QBR telemetry storyboard and action plan
author: Priya Menon
body:
Summary

This document defines a repeatable "telemetry storyboard" and actionable runbook for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with enterprise customers. The intent is to provide a concise narrative that links telemetry signals to customer outcomes, surface prioritized actions, and assign owners with deadlines. The storyboard helps Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Product leads present a coherent operational story to executive and engineering stakeholders.

Audience

- CSMs and SEs preparing QBRs for enterprise accounts
- Customer engineering and platform teams that consume telemetry
- Product and Engineering stakeholders responsible for post-QBR follow-up

Goals

1. Convert raw telemetry into a 5–7 minute operational narrative for executives.
2. Produce a prioritized action plan with owners, deadlines, and acceptance criteria.
3. Reduce time-to-resolution for top customer risks by 40% quarter-over-quarter.

Required data sources

Collect the following telemetry ahead of every QBR:

- Ingress/egress request volume (per-tenant, per-route)
- Per-request latency percentiles (P50/P90/P99) by model and sequence length
- Token-level cost and token usage by model variant
- Error rates and error class distribution (4xx vs 5xx, model fallbacks)
- Model-quality regressions from evaluation harness (monthly prompt set scores)
- Cache hit ratio (prefix / KV cache) and cache utilization trends
- Capacity allocation and reservations for Dedicated tenants
- Recent incidents and customer-impacting config changes

Data contract table (example):

| Data source | Owner | Required fields | Freshness | Retention | Query template |
|-------------|-------|-----------------|-----------|----------|----------------|
| Request logs | ingress-team | tenant_id, route, timestamp, latency_ms, model | 5m | 90d | SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id=... |
| Error stream | platform-observability | tenant_id, error_code, request_id, stack | 1m | 180d | SELECT count(*) ... |
| Cost ledger | billing | tenant_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd | 1d | 365d | SELECT SUM(cost_usd) ... |

Storyboard format

Use this short template to craft the QBR narrative. The final narrative should fit in a single slide or the first 5 minutes of the review.

1) Executive one-liner (30s):
- Current state in one sentence (health + trend + top ask). Example: "Tenant X had steady throughput in Q1 with a 12% P99 latency increase driven by larger context workloads; proposed action is to enable adaptive batching and a canary of the quantized v2 model."

2) One visual (60s):
- A single chart that ties user-visible latency or error spikes to a root cause signal (e.g., sudden increase in long-sequence requests, cache degradation, or a model rollout). Prefer overlays: request size distribution + P99 latency + cache-hit ratio.

3) Risk & impact (60s):
- Top 3 customer risks (e.g., sustained P99 > 2s on interactive routes, >10% traffic fallback to slower variants, monthly cost delta > 20% budget).
- For each risk: expected business impact and estimated cost/time to remediate.

4) Proposed actions (90s):
- Short-term (<= 2 weeks): tactical mitigations with owners and acceptance criteria.
- Medium-term (<= 3 months): config or model changes with canary plan.
- Long-term (>= 3 months): architecture or product requests (e.g., dedicated capacity increase, region expansion).

Pre-QBR checklist (to be completed 7 business days before meeting)

1. Validate data freshness from all required sources and confirm queries run without errors.
2. Create the single-chart visual and attach raw query results.
3. Run the evaluation harness on the customer prompt sample and note any regressions.
4. Confirm assigned owners and preliminary remediation estimates.
5. Send an executive summary (one-pager) to customer 3 business days before QBR.

During-QBR playbook (facilitator: CSM)

1. Opening (3 minutes): executive one-liner and agenda.
2. Data narrative (6–8 minutes): present the storyboard visual and explain causal links. Keep technical detail for the appendix.
3. Action negotiation (7–10 minutes): propose short- and medium-term actions, capture customer preferences and constraints.
4. Commitment & next steps (2–3 minutes): confirm owners, deadlines, and success criteria; schedule follow-up checkpoint within 2 weeks.

Action runbook (post-QBR)

Every action is tracked as a ticket in the customer success tracker (preferred backends: Jira project REDWOOD-CUST or internal tracker). For each action, fill in the ticket template below:

- Title: short description (e.g., "Enable adaptive batching for tenant X on route /chat")
- Owner: person/team
- Priority: P0/P1/P2
- Acceptance criteria: precise metric change and timeframe (e.g., "P99 latency reduction from 2.1s -> <=1.2s within 7 days")
- Test plan / Canary: route traffic fraction, monitoring queries, rollback trigger conditions
- ETA and dependency list

Action ticket example: priority P1, owner: infra-performance, acceptance criteria: 20% token cost reduction on inference-heavy routes measured over 72h, canary 5% of production traffic, automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5% above baseline.

Alert-to-action mapping (quick lookup)

- P99 latency spike & correlated increase in long-context requests -> Action: enable batching with max batch latency 40ms + increase KV cache TTL by 30% (Owner: serving-runtime).
- Sudden fallback to smaller model variant -> Action: investigate model-serving capacity and rollback recent deploys; if capacity constrained, route traffic to regional spare pool (Owner: infra-sre).
- Regressions in eval harness score (->3 points on customer prompt set) -> Action: open model-quality incident, pause canary rollout, and schedule rollback (Owner: applied-ml).

Example queries and dashboard snippets

- Example Prometheus/SQL pseudo query for P99 by route:
  SELECT route, percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p99_latency
  FROM request_logs
  WHERE tenant_id = 'TENANT_X' AND timestamp > now() - interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY route

- Cache hit ratio:
  SELECT SUM(cache_hits) / NULLIF(SUM(cache_hits + cache_misses),0) AS hit_ratio FROM kvcache_metrics WHERE tenant_id='TENANT_X' AND timestamp > now() - interval '14 days'

Post-QBR cadence and SLA for action closure

- Short-term actions (<=2 weeks): SLA = 14 calendar days from QBR date to implement or to produce a mitigation plan.
- Medium-term actions (<=3 months): Progressive checkpoints at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks.
- If any action exceeds SLA without customer-agreed extension, escalate to Customer Success Manager Director and Product PM.

Ownership and escalation path

- CSM: primary facilitator and owner of customer comms and ticket backlog.
- SE (solutions engineer): technical owner for on-calls to implement canaries and run tests.
- Infra/SRE: owner for capacity, routing, and network fixes.
- Applied ML/Product: owner for model-quality actions and rollbacks.

Escalation ladder:
1) Owner -> CSM
2) CSM -> SE Lead or Infra SRE on-call (if technical unblock needed)
3) CSM -> Customer Success Manager Director -> Product PM -> Head of Engineering (if cross-team commitments required)

Templates and attachments (appendix)

- Executive one-pager template (copy/paste):
  Title: QBR Executive Brief – Tenant X
  One-liner (30s): <fill>
  Visual: attach chart file
  Top 3 risks: list
  Top 3 actions: owner, ETA, acceptance criteria

- Ticket template (copy/paste):
  Summary: <short text>
  Description: <context + query links + raw results>
  Acceptance criteria: <quantified metric>
  Canary plan: <traffic % and rollback triggers>
  Attachments: <links to dashboard + raw CSVs>

Appendix: common pitfalls and mitigations

- Pitfall: Telemetry freshness mismatch. Mitigation: Run sanity queries and include raw CSVs in QBR packet; push a data contract alert to platform-observability.
- Pitfall: Overfitting to noisy P99 spikes. Mitigation: Require correlated signal (request size, cache drop, or deployment event) before actioning high-cost remediations.
- Pitfall: Customer acceptance criteria too vague. Mitigation: Convert criteria to measured SLO deltas and require a 72h verification window.
